The deployed /auth/whoami on hauska-mcp-server returns only {anonymous, jurisdiction_tenant} -- NO key_id. Any dispatch or script that expects key_id there will fail its own assertion. Link a presented key to its row via /admin/keys last_used_at instead.

A tenant-private pack answer set cannot be fully proven without a SECOND tenant-private pack to point the same key at: fixture-city is what turned 'the key works' into 'the key is tenant-scoped' (403). The dispatch expected this direction to be UNMEASURED; it was measurable, because smartcity-dashboards ships bastrop_tx AND fixture-city as tenant-private (src/city-pack.test.mjs). Check the pack list before declaring a direction unmeasurable.

Secret names are an interface and they lie. PRODUCTION_HAUSKA_MCP_URL / STAGING_HAUSKA_MCP_URL in hauska-prod-497015 hold postgresql:// DSNs with passwords. A lane looking for an HTTP URL by name will print a production database credential. Read the value only after some source other than the name says what it should contain.

gcloud secrets versions add --data-file=- reads the value from STDIN, so a minted secret can go from an HTTP response to Secret Manager without touching argv, a temp file, or a log. Pair it with a describe-first guard so a re-run of the lane cannot silently rotate a credential that other lanes are already reading.

probe-close-gate.mjs does NOT gate P-327..P-351: the registry declares OPS-24 rows [327,351] and the hook's literal range stops at 320. Its own self-test fails on that check. Until the one-line fix lands, any OPS-24 close in that range commits ungraded. Repro: node scripts/enforcement/probe-close-gate.mjs --self-test.

Run a control's own self-test when you are about to rely on it, not only when you suspect it. The gate here fails LOUD in self-test and silently in production use -- it just does not fire for rows outside its literal ranges, which is indistinguishable from 'this close had nothing to gate'. A control whose miss looks identical to a pass has to be exercised positively to be believed.
